title: Employ staff under the Sugar Industry Award 2020
what: Pay and employ staff at no less than the terms of the Sugar Industry Award 2020.

sources.title: Sugar Industry Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.1 This award covers employers throughout Australia in the sugar industry and their employees who are covered by the classifications in this award.

reach.note: National system employers that are companies, in every state.

sources.title: Sugar Industry Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.2 In this award sugar industry means the following: [4.2(a) varied by PR764072 from 11Jul23] (a) field sector : all sugar cane farming operations including the operations of contractors performing general farm work, cane harvesting and haul out work and farm management; cane testing; and pest, disease control, advisory and research operations of Cane Protection and Productivity Boards and Sugar Research Australia Limited; (b) milling sector : sugar milling including the following operations of the sugar miller: operations of transporting and processing cane including cane railway construction, maintenance, repair and operation; factory maintenance, repair and operation; raw sugar refining at a sugar mill; by-product manufacture and processing at a sugar mill; and packaging operations performed at a sugar mill; (c) refinery sector : refining raw sugar at sugar refineries and those refineries’ own packaging and storage operations; (d) distillery sector : distilling operations of sugar by-products for industrial purposes and packaging work in a distilling operation directly linked to a sugar mill;

sources.title: Which system of employment laws applies
sources.publisher: Government of Western Australia (Private Sector Labour Relations)
sources.quote: The state system covers: Private sector businesses and their employees that operate as: Sole traders. Partnerships, where none of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

assessment.summary: The Sugar Industry Award sets the industry's classifications, minimum pay, allowances and penalty rates on top of the National Employment Standards.

marks.reason: Classifications, allowances, penalty rates and their record-keeping add to the cost and complexity of employing in the industry.
